title: kv-cache: improved memory management and eviction (defrag, paging & spillover)
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and unbounded in-memory growth during mixed-length workloads caused increased OOM risk on high-concurrency serving nodes. This PR introduces a set of coordinated improvements: (1) a background defragmentation/compaction pass for hot shards, (2) a size-aware eviction policy that prefers evicting large cold entries (LRU+size), and (3) an optional paging/spillover manager that transparently moves cold KV entries to local NVMe-backed spillover storage with asynchronous rehydration. Changes are feature-flagged and tunable via the new kv_cache_config. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmarks (latency + throughput) - [x] Metrics and alerts added - [x] Feature-flag gated and off by default Implementation highlights: - new allocator implementation (shard-level slab allocator) with fragmentation tracking counters - defragmentation worker that performs in-place compaction when fragmentation > threshold - eviction_policy: LRU weight adjusted by entry size and recency; avoids evicting many small items when a single large cold item would free comparable memory - paging_manager: async spill to NVMe (configurable path), eviction records replaced with lightweight tombstones pointing to spill files; rehydration is asynchronous and capped to avoid latency spikes - added observability: kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio, kv_cache.evicted_by_size, kv_cache.spill_bytes, kv_cache.rehydrate_latency_p50/p95 - minimal public API changes: config flags and two new runtime metrics Only the runtime implementation, tests, and docs are changed; no serving API surface changes. Benchmarks: end-to-end load tests on a 16-GPU serving cluster (mixed prompt lengths) show: - peak memory usage reduced by ~18% at steady-state with defrag + size-aware eviction enabled - 99th percentile token latency increased by <2ms on median workloads when rehydration was not triggered; when rehydration occurs we fall back to a cold-hot tier policy to bound latency impact - throughput identical within noise for our canonical batching workload Backwards compatibility and rollout: feature-flagged; paging/spillover is off by default and requires local NVMe to be enabled. Rolling upgrade instructions included in docs. Risks & mitigations: rehydration can cause latency spikes; mitigated by bounded async queues + request-level fallback to a lighter-weight model variant. The description is intentionally compact; see linked Linear ticket and design doc for detailed diagrams.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Looks good overall. A couple questions: (1) what is the lock contention profile for the defrag worker under high QPS? (2) can we surface a per-shard metric for defrag work time?

Amina Shah: Added shard-level defrag_time_ms metrics and moved defrag to a low-priority worker pool. Lock contention measured <5% additional mutex hold time in our stress runs; added benchmark results to the PR description.
Priya Ramaswamy: Please add an opt-out for paging on Dedicated nodes where local NVMe is not available. Also request unit tests for tombstone behavior.
Amina Shah: Paging is feature-flagged and requires local_nvm_path in kv_cache_config; added tombstone tests and an explicit error path for missing NVMe.
Eliot Chen (approve): Verified metrics and smoke tests on a staging fleet (10 nodes). Minor nits in comments addressed. Approving to merge once CI is green.
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory efficiency by adding defragmentation, size-aware eviction, and optional NVMe spillover for cold entries. Feature-flagged; see docs/kv_cache.md for rollout instructions and tuning knobs.
benchmarks_summary: Steady-state memory reduction ~18% with defrag + size-aware eviction; 99p token latency delta <2ms when rehydration not triggered; controlled latency spikes during rehydration bounded by queue limits.
notes: Hotfix consideration: A follow-up PR will add automated alerting for spill utilization > 80% and a best-effort background reclamation policy.
